tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what this repository is: Greenstand's Apache Airflow automation for the Treetracker platform. It explains the three install paths (local, pip, docker), how DAGs are authored, and the pull-request workflow. Read this first to build a mental map before you open any Python code.

tour.title: The DAG Orchestration Pattern
tour.description: The earnings export DAG is the canonical example of this project's core pattern. An Airflow DAG file stays thin: it only defines the schedule and wires a PythonOperator to a callable that lives in the shared lib module. This separation keeps orchestration (when to run) apart from business logic (what to do), which you will see repeated across every DAG.
tour.languageLesson: Airflow DAGs use PythonOperator(task_id=..., python_callable=fn) to run a Python function as a scheduled task. The DAG object is a directed acyclic graph of such operators; default_args (retries, failure callbacks) apply to every task.

tour.title: Shared Utilities (lib/utils)
tour.description: lib/utils.py is the most depended-upon file in the project, imported by nearly every DAG and job. It centralizes Slack notifications, the task-failure callback wired into default_args, timing helpers, and month-range date math. Understand it early: once you know these helpers, the rest of the codebase reads faster.
tour.languageLesson: A Python callback like on_failure_callback passes a function reference (not a call) so Airflow invokes it later with task context. This is the same first-class-function idea PythonOperator relies on.

tour.title: An Export Job (lib/earning_export)
tour.description: Following the callable that Step 2's DAG wired up, lib/earning_export.py holds the real work: query earnings for a date range, then push the dataset to a CKAN endpoint. This is the archetypal export job. Note how it uses the date helpers from lib/utils (Step 3) and keeps all I/O and SQL in the library, not the DAG.

tour.title: A Reporting Job with PostGIS
tour.description: lib/country_leader_board.py shows the reporting flavor of a job: it runs spatial SQL (PostGIS) to count planted trees per country and writes the leader board back to the database. Compared to the export jobs in Step 4, reporting jobs compute aggregates in-database rather than shipping raw data out. This illustrates the range of logic the shared lib layer holds.

tour.title: A Migration Job
tour.description: Migration jobs reshape data rather than export or report it. migrate_stakeholders_dag.py orchestrates the consolidation using Postgres and Kubernetes pod operators, while lib/sync_entity_stakeholder.py does the transactional reconciliation of entity-stakeholder relationships, complete with a dry-run mode. This is the third major job category alongside export (Step 4) and reporting (Step 5).

tour.title: Web-Map Precompute DAGs
tour.description: The map precompute layer keeps the Greenstand web map fast. pre_request_map_clusters_dag.py schedules cache warming, and lib/pre_request_map_clusters.py pre-warms cluster tile endpoints across zoom levels by repeatedly calling the pre_request helper. This reuses the exact thin-DAG-plus-lib-callable pattern from Step 2, now applied to map tiles instead of data exports.

tour.title: Map Node.js Scripts
tour.description: Some map work runs in Node.js rather than Python. map/tile-pre-cache.py is an Airflow DAG that shells out every 5 minutes to cURL hot map tiles, while map/scripts/assign-new-trees-to-clusters.js queries newly tracked trees and assigns them to cluster regions in Postgres. This shows the project spanning two runtimes for the map subsystem.

tour.title: Cron & Shell Wrappers
tour.description: Not everything runs inside Airflow. The shell wrappers run the Node map scripts from Step 8 as cron jobs. precache.sh warms the tile-server cache by curling low-zoom tiles, and assign-new-trees-to-clusters.sh guards against overlapping runs with a PID lock file before invoking the Node task. package.json declares the HTTP dependencies those scripts need.
tour.languageLesson: A PID lock file (write $$ to a file, check it on start) prevents a slow cron job from starting a second overlapping instance. It is the shell equivalent of a mutex for scheduled tasks.

tour.title: The Test Approach
tour.description: The project tests the lib job logic, not the thin DAGs. lib/utils_test.py validates the shared date helpers from Step 3, and lib/earning_export_test.py exercises the export routine from Step 4; tutorial_test.py mirrors the tutorial DAG wiring. This confirms the design intent: because logic lives in lib and DAGs stay thin, unit tests can cover the important behavior without spinning up Airflow.
